question: m04
q: Is unemployment higher in NSW or Victoria right now, and by how much?

transcript.answer:
Unemployment is higher in **Victoria**. In September 2026, the latest month of data, Victoria's rate was **5.1%** and NSW's was **4.7%**, a gap of about **0.3 percentage points** (5.05% vs 4.71%, seasonally adjusted).

The gap has narrowed sharply because NSW jumped in September:

| Month (2026) | NSW | Victoria | Gap (Vic − NSW) |
|---|---|---|---|
| April | 4.4% | 4.8% | 0.4 pts |
| May | 4.3% | 4.9% | 0.6 pts |
| June | 4.0% | 5.1% | 1.1 pts |
| July | 4.3% | 5.1% | 0.8 pts |
| August | 4.4% | 5.2% | 0.8 pts |
| September | 4.7% | 5.1% | 0.3 pts |

- **NSW** rose 0.35 points in September (from 4.35% to 4.71%), its highest rate in this six-month period.
- **Victoria** fell slightly, from 5.17% to 5.05%. It has been the higher of the two in every month since at least April.

Monthly state figures from the ABS jump around a lot, so one month's rise in NSW may not last. Victoria has been consistently higher, but over the last few months the gap has mostly been 0.6 to 1.1 points, not the 0.3 points seen in September.
